role: Agent 1, visual systems and component coherence (finding IDs V). Simulated host only: the frozen baseline 1.7.0.0-d03 served by pi-sim with PI_SIM_PLUGIN_DIR set, headless Chrome on this Windows 10 machine with Segoe UI, lab ports 31010-31012. Evidence is in %TEMP%\hw-r3-visual\: probe.mjs (modes band, folds, states, inventory, rotation, flat, colors, narrow), probe2.mjs to probe7b.mjs, one folder of PNG and JSON per run, and cap\ from `pi-lab.mjs capture --widths 373,320 --dpr 2`.
examined: Theme band on the key and dial panels at 373x410, DPR 3: Default, explicit (Ember, Paper), inherited (Midnight), shared Paper, unknown stored value "neon", empty key. For each: resting state, keyboard focus (Tab) and pointer hover. Measured computed styles, the name line and help text, write counts (band\band.json, band-*.png)
Chip preview against the header face: sampled background pixels for Void, Paper and Midnight, and chip name, accent and label contrast for all 7 palettes (contrast.py)

Fold states (default, all folded, all open) on key-configured, dial-configured, dial-groups, control-reset, key-empty and dial-empty: band position, fold-pair aria-disabled, opacity and tab order, writes (folds\folds.json)

Data states at 373x410: missing, unavailable, stale, holding, healthy Gadget, alert, Back tile, empty key and dial, plus forced single source with unavailable HWiNFO. Measured status block, band position and header text (states\, p2\forced.json)

Style inventory with every disclosure open (font sizes, weights, colours, radii, borders, control heights) for key-configured, key-dense, key-details, dial-groups, dial-custom-gestures, control-reset and slot-reading (inventory\inventory.json)
Grouped and flat rotation editor: focus treatment on list, chip and toolbar, glyphs, help lines and their line counts, box height (rotation\rotation.json, rot-*.png)
Group remove control: one click and a double click, reproduced with real CDP mouse events (p5\group-remove*.json)
Reading colour wells and Auto buttons under Void, Paper and Ember, with and without one colour set (colors\colors.json)

Zoom and other widths: 189x410, 160x410, 320x560 and 380x720 for key, dial, dial-groups and control. Measured header and band rectangles, elements past the viewport edge, cut text (narrow\narrow.json, p3\overflow.json)
Keyboard Tab audit with all sections open on the key, dial-groups and Control panels: whether each focus ring gets clipped (p6\focus.json)
Emulated forced-colors: active through CDP, not real High Contrast: band, folded sections, rotation (p7\)

Candidate fixes tried by injecting CSS at runtime in the lab only (nothing written to any repo): color-scheme dark, and a Default chip frame and link mark drawn in the chip's own palette colours (p4\)
Detail tile editor (key-details) and the Control and detail-tile headers (p2\details.json, p2\control-*.png, slot-*.png)

Code read: sensor-reading.html, sensor-dial.html, control.html, detail-slot.html, pi.css (all of it), pi-shell.js (all of it), and in pi-common.js the theme gallery, rotation editor and reading colours; the e2e assertions on the band in scripts/e2e-pi-panels.mjs:420-470; src/ui/state-screens.ts:90-110

Lab caveat: on Windows, scripts/lib/cdp.mjs close() stops only the launcher process. The Chrome browser it spawned keeps running and holds the debugging port, so a later lab on the same port can attach to the stale browser. I found six such process trees on my port 31012 and stopped them; leftovers on other agents' ports were not touched. I then reran the band and states probes on a clean browser and got identical numbers

findings.title: Group remove x deletes a group in one press; a double-click deletes the next group too
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups fixture (groups CPU [Tctl, CCD1] and GPU [GPU Temperature, Hot Spot]); task: tidy or rename groups; 373x410 at DPR 2 on the simulated host, frozen baseline 1.7.0.0-d03
findings.observed: The group's remove control is a borderless muted x (28x28, #b8b8b8) 4 px right of the group name field, where a text field's clear button conventionally sits. One click removes the group and its readings from the rotation. There is no confirmation and no undo. After the rebuild, focus stays on a remove button that now belongs to the next group ('Remove group 1'), and that button sits under the pointer at the same point. A double-click therefore removed both groups: rotationKeys [], rotationGroups [], 4 writes, focus dropped to body. Side note for the settings-integrity reviewer: a single removal made 2 writes.
findings.evidence: MEASURED with %TEMP%\hw-r3-visual\probe5.mjs. Single click: groups [CPU,GPU] became [GPU], 2 writes, activeElement 'Remove group 1; its readings leave the rotation', and elementFromPoint(347,257) after the rebuild is that same button (p5\group-remove.json). SECOND=1 double click: groups [], chips [], 4 writes, no Undo control (p5\group-remove-twice.json, group-remove-hover.png). READ pi-common.js:640-647 (the x is a glyph with only a tooltip and an aria-label), pi-common.js:3980-3993 (removes on click, no confirm), pi-common.js:576-589 (focus is restored to .hw-group-remove[data-group="0"], which after the rebuild is the neighbouring group's button).
findings.affected_user: Power users with rotation groups: mouse users who double-click, keyboard users who press Enter twice
findings.correction: Reuse the product's existing two-step pattern for destructive actions (Replace shared settings asks for a second click; the .hw-btn[data-armed] style is at pi.css:898-901). The first press arms the control and shows words ('Remove group?') in the danger style. A second press removes. Any other click, a blur or a rebuild disarms it. After a removal, move focus to the next group's name field or to Add group, never onto another remove button.
findings.tradeoff: One more press for a rare action. E2e flows that remove a group with one click need updating. The armed control is wider and may wrap the group head at 189 px. The armed state must never carry over to another group after a rebuild.
findings.acceptance_test: In dial-groups at 373x410: (1) a double-click on group 1's remove leaves both groups and all four readings, with zero writes; (2) arming then confirming removes exactly one group; (3) afterwards document.activeElement is not a .hw-group-remove; (4) pressing Enter twice on a focused remove never removes two groups.

findings.title: Header and rotation layout break at the zoom widths (189 and 160 px): words break mid-word, the dial face is clipped, horizontal overflow
findings.area: Pinned header (key, dial) and grouped rotation editor
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured, dial-configured and dial-groups at 189x410 and 160x410 (the 378 and 320 panels at 200% zoom), DPR 2
findings.observed: The kind line and the fold pair share the text column beside the face. At 189 px that column is about 52 px wide and the pair takes 50, so 'Sensor Reading key' breaks mid-word. At 160 px it stacks one letter per line: the key header is 476 px tall, taller than the 410 px panel, and the palette starts at y 476. The dial face is a 112 px image inside a figure that is allowed to shrink, so it starts 10 px (189) and 16 px (160) left of the viewport and its left edge (the 'session' label, row names) is cut off. The grouped rotation hint 'Select one to move, rename or remove it' is cut off without an ellipsis, and the document is 58 to 87 px wider than the viewport (hidden by overflow-x).
findings.evidence: MEASURED: narrow\narrow.json (key at 160: header 476 px, kind line width 0, cut ['Sensor Reading key']; dial-groups at 160: header 285 px); p3\overflow.json (face-img left -10 and -16; .hw-set-tools-slot right edge 247 at viewport widths 189 and 160); narrow-key-configured-160x410.png, narrow-dial-groups-160x410.png, narrow-dial-groups-189x410.png, p3\dial-groups-189-rotation.png. READ: pi.css:87-93 (the header never wraps); pi.css:141-152 (dial figure is flex 0 1 auto with min-width 0); pi.css:192-235 (the fold pair sits in the kind line, and the 199 px media query only shrinks the buttons); pi.css:1380-1401 (the slot has no min-width: 0, so the nowrap hint sets its min-content width). The earlier REPORT checked only the chips at 160 px.
findings.affected_user: Low-vision users who zoom the panel
findings.correction: Change only below about 240 px, through a media query. Let the header wrap (.hw-head { flex-wrap: wrap }) so the text column moves under the face; the header is unpinned at these widths anyway. Alternatively, give the fold pair its own row. Stop the dial figure from shrinking below its image (flex: none, or align-items: flex-start). Add min-width: 0 to .hw-set-tools-slot so the hint ellipsizes as its own comment intends.
findings.tradeoff: At zoom the header gets taller but its words stay readable. The change must be scoped by the media query so 373 and 320 stay pixel-identical. --hw-head-h and the pin-off rule re-measure.
findings.acceptance_test: At 189x410 and 160x410 on the key, dial and Control panels: no header word breaks inside a word (the kind line uses at most two lines), face-img left >= 0, documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth, and the slot hint ends in an ellipsis. At 373x410 and 320x560, every header and band rectangle is unchanged.

findings.title: Default chip's link mark and dashed frame all but vanish when the shared theme is Paper
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured and dial-configured with the shared theme set to Paper and Default selected, 373x410 at DPR 3; compared with the other six palettes
findings.observed: The link mark is always the panel's link blue #8ecbff and the dashed frame always the panel's muted #b8b8b8, whatever palette the Default face shows. On the Paper face (#E9E6DE) the mark measures 1.39:1 and the frame 1.59:1, so Default reads as a second Paper chip with faint grey dashes. On the six dark palettes the mark measures 9.8 to 12.1:1 and the frame 8.6 to 10.6:1.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: band\band.json (paper-shared-default: badge rgb(142,203,255) on face rgb(233,230,222); face border 2px dashed rgb(184,184,184)); ratios from contrast.py; band-paper-shared-default.png, band-dial-paper-shared.png. READ: pi.css:440-451 (the band badge has no background), pi.css:1550-1552 (frame colour), pi.css:1556-1566 (badge colour var(--hw-link)). Standard: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for graphics needed to understand a control. The word 'Default' still carries the identity, so this breaks contract 1 ('Default keeps its link mark') in practice more than it strictly fails 1.4.11.
findings.affected_user: Anyone whose shared theme is Paper, low-vision users most
findings.correction: Draw both marks in the palette the chip shows. Colour the badge with the palette's value colour, the same inline colour the chip name already gets (pi-common.js:3447). Draw the frame 1px dashed in the palette's label colour, which measures 5.2 to 7.4:1 on every face. A runtime lab injection that used the value colour for both is in p4\defaultfix-paper.png and defaultfix-void.png: the mark and frame are clearly visible on Paper.
findings.tradeoff: The mark loses its fixed blue and reads as part of the chip rather than a panel accent. The 1px frame is quieter than today, which is intended (see V03). It must still render correctly in forced colours, where the face has forced-color-adjust: none.
findings.acceptance_test: With each of the 7 palettes as the shared theme, the Default chip's glyph and frame measure at least 3:1 against its face (at least 7:1 on Paper), and every chip name stays whole at 373, 320, 189 and 160 px.

findings.title: The theme name line reports the hovered or focused chip in the same style as the real selection
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured (Default selected, key draws Void) with the pointer resting on Paper; a stored unknown theme 'neon' with Tab into the group; 373x410
findings.observed: Hovering Paper turns 'Theme Default · Void' into 'Theme Paper', in the same bold style as a real choice. Meanwhile the key still draws Void and the help line under the chips still says 'Default follows the shared theme.' With 'neon' stored, Tab lands on Default (the group's only Tab stop) and the line changes from '"neon" · draws Void' to 'Default · Void', although Default is not checked and the help line still says the key stores 'neon'. Every chip now shows its name, so the preview only repeats the text already under the pointer. Zero writes.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: band.log (the hover line reads 'Paper' in 8 of 9 cases and 'Void' when Paper is chosen; unknown-stored focus line reads 'Default · Void'); band-void-default-hover-paper.png, band-unknown-stored-focus.png. READ: pi-common.js:3485-3499 and 3577-3592. This behaviour is asserted by scripts/e2e-pi-panels.mjs:441-445.
findings.affected_user: Everyone who reads the line while pointing at chips; keyboard users when a newer version's theme is stored
findings.correction: Make the line state only what is stored and drawn: renderThemeLine uses themeOverride only, and the pointerover and focusin preview is dropped. Hover feedback stays on the chip itself.
findings.tradeoff: This changes a tested behaviour, so the e2e check 'focus on a swatch names it without picking it' must be updated. No information is lost, because each chip shows its own name.
findings.acceptance_test: With Default · Void selected, hovering or focusing any chip leaves #theme-current reading 'Default · Void'. With 'neon' stored, Tab focus keeps '"neon" · draws Void'. Zero writes.

findings.title: The band repeats 'Default' and the panel uses three different ways to say 'inherited'
findings.area: Theme band plus Display select and summary wording
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured and key-inherited (shared Midnight, shared text Dimmed), 373x410, folded and open
findings.observed: Within the 125 px band, 'Default' appears three times (name line, chip, help line) and the resolved theme is named once. The panel says 'inherited' three different ways: the band's 'Default · Midnight', the Text color select's 'Default (shared: Dimmed)', and the Display summary's 'theme text (shared)'. The help line costs about 20 px to restate what the chip and name line already say.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: band\band.json (line and help text), folds\folds.json (summaries), cap\key-inherited--default--373.png. READ: pi-common.js:3485-3530 and 3598-3606.
findings.affected_user: Beginners learning what inheritance means; everyone, for height
findings.correction: Use one line, in the idiom the Text color select already uses: 'Theme  Default (shared: Void)  Change' when following the shared theme, 'Theme  Ember (this key only)' when chosen here. Drop the help line in those two states and keep it only where it adds a fact (no reading picked yet, or an unknown stored value). Keep 'Change' outside the span that ellipsizes.
findings.tradeoff: The band drops to about 105 px and everything below it moves up 20 px, so the density baselines, the e2e y-assertions and the help-text check (e2e-pi-panels.mjs:437) change. The sentence 'Default follows the shared theme' goes; '(shared: Void)' plus 'Change' carries it. At 160 px the line must still keep 'Change' visible.
findings.acceptance_test: In key-configured at 373x410: 'Default' appears at most twice in the band (chip and line); the resolved theme is visible without hovering; the band is at most 108 px tall and the same height for all eight picks; the 24 px 'Change' target is fully visible at 373, 320, 189 and 160 px.

findings.title: Reading colour wells show white for Automatic in every theme; disabled Auto buttons look enabled
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups with Reading colors on Automatic, under Void, Paper and Ember, and with one well set to #ff7e8e; 373x410 at DPR 2
findings.observed: Every automatic well shows #ffffff whatever the theme. Under Paper the face directly above draws the numbers near-black (#14120D); under Ember it draws them orange (#FFB84D). The four Auto buttons are disabled when their row is already automatic, but they render exactly like an enabled button: #ececec text, #3a3a3a fill, #7c7c7c border, pointer cursor, opacity 1. After one colour is set, only one of the four does anything, with no visual difference.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: colors\colors.json; colors-paper.png compared with colors-paper-face.png; colors-one-set.png. READ: pi-common.js:3348 (well.value = color ?? '#FFFFFF'), pi-common.js:3361 (reset.disabled); pi.css:866-886 has no :disabled rule for .hw-reading-colors button (compare .hw-set-tools button[aria-disabled] at pi.css:1431-1436 and .hw-support:disabled at pi.css:926-929).
findings.affected_user: Power users setting per-reading colours, especially on Paper or Ember
findings.correction: (1) Show the automatic state truthfully. Either seed the well with the colour the dial actually draws, using the same resolver the dial uses (the text-colour wells already seed from the theme via themeValueSeed() at pi-common.js:3643-3650), or show a neutral 'auto' swatch. Display only, never written. (2) Give disabled buttons one look across the panel, the rotation toolbar's: muted text, rule-coloured border, no fill, default cursor.
findings.tradeoff: Seeding from the theme's value colour is still wrong when 'Color numbers by sensor type' applies, so either follow the dial's resolver or use the neutral swatch. A native colour input cannot show 'no colour', so the neutral swatch needs a small wrapper.
findings.acceptance_test: Under Paper, no automatic well shows #ffffff. Disabled Auto buttons differ from enabled ones in text colour and border and use the default cursor. Opening the panel makes zero writes.

findings.title: Status blocks push the palette off the first screen, and healthy Gadget keeps a 5-line block
findings.area: Status block under the header (key and dial)
findings.state_task_viewport: key and dial unavailable with Data source set to 'Gadget registry only'; key-unavailable, key-stale, key-missing; key-configured running on Gadget (healthy); 373x410
findings.observed: The status block under the header is 80 to 239 px tall. With a forced source and no HWiNFO, the palette spans y 336 to 461 on the key and 352 to 477 on the dial, so it falls below the 410 px panel, and the three buttons wrap to two rows. The first sentence (the plugin hint) tells the person to enable Shared Memory Support; the very next line says Shared Memory is never read. In the healthy Gadget state, a 5-line (96 px) info block about producer timestamps and stable hardware IDs sits above the palette every time the panel opens.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: p2\forced.json and p2\dial-unavail-gadget-only.png; states\states.json (status block heights 116, 153, 136, 80 and 96 px; palette tops at y 213, 250, 233, 177 and 193), states\state-key-gadget.png. READ: pi-shell.js:571-586 (hint, forced-source line, reassurance, 2 to 3 buttons) and 619-621 (info hint shown in a healthy state); src/ui/state-screens.ts:95 and 104 (hint copy, plugin side).
findings.affected_user: Gadget users (the free-HWiNFO path) on every open; everyone during outages
findings.correction: Keep the block where it is and tighten it. When a source is forced, replace the generic hint with the source-specific sentence instead of adding one. Cut the reassurance to one clause ('Your reading and settings stay saved.'). Use short action words that fit one row ('Retry', 'Setup steps', 'Data source'). In the healthy Gadget state show one line ('Gadget registry: current values only, no min, max or average.') and move the rest to Connection, or behind a 'Why' disclosure there.
findings.tradeoff: Less teaching inline during outages. The hint strings live plugin-side in src/ui/state-screens.ts, fall under the release copy rules and validate-release-copy, and the docs may need to match.
findings.acceptance_test: At 373x410, in every fixture state including forced-source unavailable, both chip rows end at or above y 410. The healthy Gadget status is one line (about 36 px including padding). A forced-source outage never advises enabling Shared Memory.

findings.title: Two reorder editors with two visual dialects (rotation list vs detail list)
findings.area: Dial rotation editor vs key Press > custom detail list
findings.state_task_viewport: key-details (custom list, all sections open) compared with dial-configured and dial-groups rotation; 373x410
findings.observed: The rotation editor uses selectable chips, one worded 28 px toolbar with left and right arrows for Earlier and Later, and the neutral colour tokens. The detail list puts inline, glyph-only 24 px up, down and x buttons on every chip. It has a 'x2' size button next to the x remove button in the same tile, so the same glyph means 'remove' and 'size' side by side. Its '+' buttons carry their meaning ('Send the next picks into tile 2') only in the aria-label and tooltip. It uses its own blue-grey colours (#2c313a, #56606c, #6d7a8a, #dde3ea, #9aa3ae) outside the token set. The same concept, earlier and later in a wrapping row, points left and right in one editor and up and down in the other.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: p2\details.json (sizes, colours, labels), p2\detail-editor.png, rotation\rot-flat-rest.png, inventory\inventory.json (the #56606c and #555 borders appear only on key-details). READ: pi.css:1682-1755 and 1202-1248.
findings.affected_user: Power users who configure both detail lists and dial rotations
findings.correction: A small change with no restructuring: move the detail editor onto the panel tokens (--hw-field, --hw-edge, --hw-text, --hw-muted); replace 'x2' with words that cannot be read as remove, such as '2 cells' (the aria text already says this); use left and right move glyphs as the rotation toolbar does. Unifying both on one listbox-plus-toolbar pattern is a larger decision for later.
findings.tradeoff: The size button gets about 20 px wider, so tiles wrap sooner at 320. Any e2e check that matches glyph text needs to match the labels instead.
findings.acceptance_test: Inside #detail-list, no colour falls outside the :root tokens (face and theme colours excepted); no visible x appears on a control that does not remove; both editors use the same pair of move glyphs.

findings.title: Native checkboxes and radios render in the light scheme and outshine their checked state
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups (group radios, 'Color numbers by sensor type'), key-configured ('°F'), all at 373x410, DPR 2
findings.observed: The page declares no color-scheme (computed value 'normal'), so unchecked checkboxes and radios paint white, at 13.8:1 against the panel. They are the brightest marks on the panel after the face and the Paper chip. The unchecked group radio (a white disc) is louder than the checked one (a blue ring), which inverts the emphasis of 'which group receives new ticks'. In the inline checklists, every unchecked row shows a white box.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: p2\scheme.json ({html: 'normal'}), rotation\rot-focus-list1.png. Injecting :root { color-scheme: dark } at runtime in the lab renders them dark grey while the checked state stays blue (p4\scheme-after-rotation.png compared with scheme-before-rotation.png). INFERRED for the real host: Chromium 130 in QtWebEngine 6.9 paints unstyled form controls the same way when no scheme is declared; not seen on the bench.
findings.correction: Add color-scheme: dark to :root in pi.css. The checked state is already styled with accent-color.
findings.tradeoff: This also darkens native select popups, the colour-picker chrome and autofill, and any scrollbar parts the sdpi styles do not cover. It must be checked once in the real app (Stream Deck 7.4.2).
findings.acceptance_test: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).colorScheme === 'dark'; an unchecked checkbox or radio is less prominent against the panel than the checked one; in the real app, select popups render dark.

findings.title: In forced colours, the section disclosure triangles become bars

findings.title: About ten lines of help around the grouped rotation editor, with two instructions said twice

findings.title: The header names only reading 1 on multi-reading keys and ignores the dial's rotation names

findings.title: Theme band frames: the unselected Default frame competes with the selection ring, and focus adds a third frame
findings.state_task_viewport: key-custom-dim (Ember chosen) and key-configured (Default chosen) with Tab focus, 373x410 at DPR 3
findings.observed: When another theme is chosen, two chips wear a 2 px high-contrast frame: Default's dashed #b8b8b8 (10.6:1 against its black face) and the chosen chip's #ececec ring (11.7:1 against the panel). At a glance both read as marked. With keyboard focus on Default, three concentric frames sit within about 7 px: the blue focus ring, the white selection ring and the dashed frame. Focus and selection never disagree in this radio group (arrow keys pick), so the stack adds no information.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: band-ember-explicit.png, band-void-default-focus.png; band.json (selection outline '2px solid rgb(236,236,236) off 1px', focus outline '2px solid rgb(124,196,255)'). READ: pi.css:1539-1543, 1550-1552 and 67-70.
findings.affected_user: Everyone, beginners checking which theme is on
findings.correction: The same change as V02 (a 1px dashed frame in the palette's label colour) leaves the selection ring as the only 2 px frame in the band; see the lab injection in p4\defaultfix-ember-explicit.png. Leave the focus ring as it is: it is the panel's one focus treatment.

findings.title: Back-tile role note runs edge to edge and uses the warning look for neutral information
findings.area: Key panel, Back tile role note
findings.observed: The role note spans x 0 to 373 while every status block is inset to x 12 to 361. It also wears the warning look (amber bar, brown fill) although it is neutral information. Cause: .hw-hint (pi.css:811-826) comes after .hw-lede (pi.css:319-322) with equal specificity, so its margin of 8px 0 0 wins.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: states\states.json (key-back role note at [0, 97, 373, 64] vs key-missing status at [12, 97, 349, 116]); states\state-key-back.png.
findings.correction: Add .hw-hint.hw-lede { margin: var(--hw-s2) var(--hw-gutter) 0; } and give the role note the info tone (--hw-info-bg, no amber bar). Keep the warning tone for real warnings (layout-hint, detail-unsupported).
findings.tradeoff: Only the Back tile's first screen changes: the note becomes 24 px narrower.
findings.acceptance_test: In key-back, the role note's rect has left 12 and width 349, and its background equals --hw-info-bg.

findings.title: Four icon languages across one panel
findings.observed: The panel mixes four icon styles: Lucide strokes (the fold pair and the link mark); a font glyph for Reload (U+27F3); CSS border triangles for disclosures (grey for sections, link blue for the 'How' disclosures); and text arrows and x in the rotation toolbar, where three of the four buttons carry a glyph and Rename has none. The detail editor adds its own up, down, grip and + glyphs.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: rotation\rotation.json (glyphs), captures. READ: sensor-reading.html:56; pi-common.js:473-478; pi.css:255-266, 523-533 and 615-622.
findings.correction: Draw Reload with Lucide rotate-cw at the fold pair's stroke (NOTICE.md already credits Lucide). Drop the leading glyphs from the rotation toolbar so the words carry it, or keep only the arrows and drop the x. Keep the CSS disclosure triangles.
findings.tradeoff: One more inline SVG. Toolbar buttons get 12 to 14 px narrower each, so they wrap less at zoom.
findings.acceptance_test: No text glyph is the only visible label of a control, and the rotation toolbar buttons are either all without glyphs or all with them.

findings.title: Row rhythm: reading 1's label is out of column, and °F sits in different places on key and dial
findings.observed: Readings 2 to 4 sit as [picker | 108 px label], but reading 1 has a full-width picker with its label below it beside the layout select, so the four labels do not share one column. The Temperature °F box sits at the right edge on the key (a row of three) and mid-row on the dial (two items in the same three-track grid). The gap between a status block and the band's 'Theme' line is 6 px, against 8 px above the block.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: crop-dense-top.png, cap\dial-groups--default--373.png, states\state-key-stale.png. READ: sensor-reading.html:62-76 and 80-92; pi.css:695-700 and 348.
findings.correction: When the layout shows more than one reading, render slot 1 like the others ([Reading 1 | Label 1]) and put 'Readings on this key' on its own row above slot 2. Give the dial's row a two-track grid with °F aligned right.
findings.tradeoff: Switching layouts would then move the label field between two positions. Alternatively, leave the single-reading layout as it is and accept the difference.
findings.acceptance_test: In key-dense, the four label inputs share one left x coordinate.
